findings.title: Missing React key on GrafanaRuleListItem in list map
findings.body: The old GrafanaRuleLoader usage passed key={key}. The new GrafanaRuleListItem element in the map has no key, while the other branches do. This triggers React key warnings and can cause incorrect reconciliation and state mix-ups, for example dropdown or modal state attached to the wrong row, when the rule list is appended to or reordered.

findings.title: Silence drawer never renders when only promRule is provided
findings.body: The silence drawer only renders when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true. In the list view `rule` is undefined and only promRule is passed. The menu now shows 'Silence notifications' based on prom-rule abilities, but clicking it sets state and nothing opens. The silence action is silently broken in the list view.

findings.title: Delete menu item hidden for prom-only rules
findings.body: The menu renders Delete only when `canDelete && rulerRule`. In the list view rulerRule is undefined, so Delete never appears even for users with permission. handleDelete also requires a RulerRuleDTO. The Delete action is lost from the list view. Similarly, the Pause item requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`, so it never renders for prom-only rules.

findings.title: Silence ability ignores recording rule and folder loading checks
findings.body: For prom rules, Silence is `[silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]`. The ruler version also required the folder to be loaded and the rule to be a Grafana alerting rule. When rule is undefined (skipToken), `useCanSilenceInFolder(undefined)` may still grant access via the global AlertingInstanceCreate permission. Combined with the OR in AlertRuleMenu, this is harmless only because isAlertingRule is false for undefined, so it is fragile.
